components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (Node.js 22.23.3)

inventory.summary: The inventory of cryptographic assets in the Ghost codebase consists primarily of JWT signing and verification (RSA-RS256/RS512 and HMAC-HS256), hashing for asset integrity (SHA-256), and non-security usages of MD5 for cache keys and ETags. RSA signatures are used for member tokens and identity tokens, which are quantum-vulnerable. Dependency inventory reveals the presence of various cryptographic libraries (jose, jsonwebtoken, elliptic, tweetnacl) and algorithms (ECDSA, ECDH, X25519). Most other sightings were identified as test fixtures or non-security UI/utility functions.

remediation.impact: Digest grows to 48 B. SHA-384 rather than SHA-256 because CNSA 2.0 requires it and the cost difference is negligible on 64-bit hardware.
remediation.why: MD5 is collision-broken or worse, which breaks signature and certificate integrity regardless of the signing algorithm.

collected.name: Token contents read before, or instead of, verifying the signature (ghost/core/core/server/services/auth/api-key/admin.js)

remediation.alternative: ML-DSA-87 where CNSA 2.0 applies; FN-DSA-512 (FIPS 206, draft) where signature size dominates and 666 B is the deciding number
remediation.impact: Public key 1,952 B and signature 3,309 B, against 64 B and 72 B for ECDSA P-256. Certificate chains grow by roughly 4 kB per link, which is what makes PQ certificates a TLS record-size and DNS-response problem before it is a CPU problem.
remediation.why: Classical signatures are a deadline problem rather than a harvesting one: a signature forged in 2035 cannot retroactively compromise a 2026 session. Migrate on a schedule, after the key exchange work.

remediation.impact: Negligible on 64-bit hardware; SHA-384 is frequently faster than SHA-256 there because it uses 64-bit words.
remediation.why: Grover gives only a square-root speedup on preimages, so hashes are not urgent. CNSA 2.0 nonetheless requires a 384-bit digest for national security systems.

collected.name: RSA in use: classical, broken by Shor (ghost/core/core/server/models/settings.js)

remediation.alternative: X25519+ML-KEM-768 where a hybrid is wanted; ML-KEM-1024 where CNSA 2.0 applies
remediation.impact: ML-KEM is a KEM and not a drop-in for RSA-OAEP: it derives a shared secret rather than encrypting a caller's plaintext, so the call site becomes encapsulate-then-AEAD (KEM/DEM). That is a redesign of the call, not a parameter change — which is the real cost here and the reason to start early.
remediation.why: Key transport, not signing: the session key is encrypted to the recipient's public key, so a ciphertext recorded today is readable once a CRQC exists. Harvestable, like key agreement, and unlike a signature.

remediation.alternative: ML-KEM-1024 alone where CNSA 2.0 applies and hybrid is not permitted
remediation.impact: ClientHello grows past 1,400 B and no longer fits one packet — which breaks middleboxes that assume it does, and requires capture snaplen of 0 to inventory. Hybrid keeps the classical half, so a flaw in ML-KEM does not leave the connection naked.
remediation.why: Classical key establishment is retroactively breakable: traffic recorded today is readable once a CRQC exists. This is the only risk class where waiting costs something already.
